I choose: Four days in the office

One reason is that while fully remote work can be highly productive, the additional four days in the office can significantly enhance team collaboration and culture, which are crucial for maintaining high output over the long term. The in-person interaction can lead to better idea sharing, quicker problem-solving, and stronger team bonds, all of which contribute to higher overall productivity.

I choose: Fully remote

One reason for this choice is that the 2026 Stanford study of 1,600 engineers showed that isolation scores were no higher for remote workers compared to those working four days in the office, once team rituals were held constant. Additionally, remote workers had 33% lower attrition rates, indicating higher job satisfaction and retention. These factors suggest that fully remote work can maintain team cohesion and productivity without the drawbacks associated with in-office attendance policies.
